metaDescription: Four Govee smart plugs compared, from the basic WiFi and Bluetooth plug to dual-outlet and energy-monitoring models, with who each one suits best.
introParagraphs: Govee is better known for lighting, but its smart plugs follow the same idea: easy app control, a Bluetooth backup and voice commands through Alexa or Google Assistant. The range is small and easy to read once you know the differences. Most of the choosing comes down to three questions: do you need two outlets covered by one plug, do you want to see how much power a device uses, and how many plugs do you actually need.

The lineup in this guide has four distinct designs. There is the standard plug, a dual plug that squeezes two outlets into the footprint of one, a 15A model aimed at group control, and an energy-monitoring version that reports live figures in the app. Several of them are sold in one, two and four plug counts, which are the same product at different quantities.

We evaluated all four from their product specs and buyer feedback. Each one uses the Govee Home app and works with Alexa and Google Assistant, so the differences below are about hardware and extras rather than ecosystems.

products.name: Govee Smart Plug with Energy Monitoring
products.description:
The Govee Smart Plug with Energy Monitoring takes the basic plug and adds real-time readouts. The Govee Home app displays the power, current and voltage of whatever is plugged in, so you can see what a fan, a lamp or a small appliance is actually drawing. That is the clearest reason to pick it over the simpler models in this family.

Connection uses both Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, which the listing says keeps access easy even when you are away. Voice control works with Alexa and Google Assistant, so the same commands you use for lights can switch the plug. Setting a routine such as a morning coffee maker start is a matter of one app schedule.

The tradeoff is that monitoring adds complexity that a lamp owner may never use, and the data stays inside the Govee app. Compared with the Govee Smart Plug 4 Pack, which is the plain version, this model offers more insight for the same basic control. Next to the Govee Dual Smart Plug it does not save outlet space, so it suits people who care about numbers more than footprint.
products.bestFor: Anyone curious about what their devices actually draw.

WiFi and Bluetooth for easier access

Available in one, two and four plug counts
cons: Monitoring is wasted on a simple lamp

products.name: Govee Smart Plug 4 Pack
products.description:
This is the standard Govee plug and the one most buyers should consider first. It connects over Wi-Fi or Bluetooth, and the listing says that combination is faster and more stable than Wi-Fi only plugs. Voice commands work with Alexa and Google Assistant.

Schedules let you build routines that switch lamps or fans automatically, and the group controller lets you bundle several plugs under one command. That makes it a natural fit for holiday strings and a living room with multiple lamps. The cost of simplicity is that it offers no energy readout and covers a single socket like a conventional plug.

In ownership terms, the four plug count gives you room to expand later. It is cheaper to run than the Govee Smart Plug with Energy Monitoring in terms of complexity, since there is nothing to configure beyond schedules. Compared with the Govee Dual Smart Plug, it is the better choice when you have only one device per outlet and no tight spacing issue.
products.bestFor: Homes that want simple, reliable control of several lamps.
pros: WiFi plus Bluetooth for steadier pairing
Group controller bundles many plugs together
Works with Alexa and Google Assistant
One, two and four plug counts available
cons: No energy usage readout in the app
Covers a full socket like any standard plug

products.name: Govee Dual Smart Plug
products.description:
The Govee Dual Smart Plug solves a problem that standard smart plugs create. It houses two horizontally positioned plugs, so it only covers a single outlet in a normal vertical fixture, which leaves the other outlet free. Each unit gives you two smart controlled sockets from one wall slot.

It has a 15A rating and uses the Govee Home app over Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, with Alexa and Google Assistant voice control. The listing notes that a couple of conditions apply to voice use, so read the setup notes before assuming every feature works the first time. The design pays off in places where you have a lamp and a charger or two lamps sharing one outlet.

Ownership is straightforward, though the larger body is something to measure against your furniture. Against the Govee Smart Plug 4 Pack, this one gets you twice the controlled devices per outlet, and next to the Govee Smart Plug 15A Group Control it trades some group emphasis for density. It is the pick for crowded walls rather than whole-home automation.
products.bestFor: Crowded outlets where two devices need smart control.

products.name: Govee Smart Plug 15A Group Control
products.description:
The Govee Smart Plug 15A Group Control is a 15A plug that focuses on connectivity and bundling. Like the other Govee models it uses the Govee Home app over Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, and the listing frames the Bluetooth link as the more stable option. Voice commands run through Alexa or Google Home, so a few spoken words switch a group.

Its selling point is remote group control, which lets you run a collection of plugs as a single scene. Custom schedules sit alongside it, so you can have patio lights and a lamp start and stop together. The compromise is that it has no energy monitoring and no dual outlet design, so it is a conventional plug with a higher rating.

At home, it behaves much like the Govee Smart Plug 4 Pack, only with a stated 15A figure on the listing. Compared with the Govee Smart Plug with Energy Monitoring, it provides no usage data. Choose it when the main goal is orchestrating many devices rather than measuring or condensing them.
products.bestFor: Decorators and multi-lamp rooms that want one command for many plugs.
pros: Stated 15A rating for everyday small appliances
Remote group control for scenes of plugs
Alexa and Google Home voice control
cons: Looks and behaves like the basic model

buyingCriteria.explanation: Energy monitoring is a feature, not a requirement, and only some Govee plugs have it. The Govee Smart Plug with Energy Monitoring reports power, current and voltage in the app. The Govee Smart Plug 4 Pack and Govee Smart Plug 15A Group Control have no readout. Pay for it if you want to understand what a device uses or to catch a device that wastes power while idle.

A normal plug covers one socket, while a dual design makes room. The Govee Dual Smart Plug places two plugs horizontally so it covers only a single outlet in a vertical fixture. That is valuable when your wall has just one free duplex and two devices to control. If you only need one device per outlet, a standard plug like the Govee Smart Plug 4 Pack is simpler.

Every Govee model here supports both Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. The Bluetooth path helps pairing and lets you reach a plug nearby even when the router is struggling. It does not replace Wi-Fi for control away from home. The listing for the Govee Smart Plug 4 Pack describes the combination as more stable than Wi-Fi-only plugs, which is a useful tiebreaker against other brands.

Groups matter once you have more than a couple of plugs. The Govee Smart Plug 15A Group Control and the Govee Smart Plug 4 Pack both advertise group control, so you can switch a set of lamps with one tap or one spoken line. Build groups by room or by purpose, not by plug count. A well-named group turns four separate controls into one clear button.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Amp rating and what you plug in
buyingCriteria.explanation: Check the rating against your appliance. The Govee Dual Smart Plug and the Govee Smart Plug 15A Group Control list 15A, which is fine for lamps, fans and small appliances. Avoid space heaters and other heat-heavy devices unless the plug clearly covers them. A monitoring plug like the Govee Smart Plug with Energy Monitoring can help you spot an unexpectedly hungry device.

Govee sells most models in one, two and four plug counts. Buy the count that matches your devices, because spares in a drawer do not help. The Govee Smart Plug 4 Pack suits a whole floor, while a single Govee Smart Plug with Energy Monitoring is enough to test one appliance. Add more later, since they all share the same app.

howWeEvaluated.title: Feature differentiation
howWeEvaluated.description: Because all four share the app and voice support, we looked at what sets each apart. The Govee Smart Plug with Energy Monitoring adds usage data, the Govee Dual Smart Plug adds a second socket, and the Govee Smart Plug 15A Group Control emphasizes bundles. The Govee Smart Plug 4 Pack is the baseline.

howWeEvaluated.title: Connection reliability
howWeEvaluated.description: Based on product specs and buyer feedback, we credited the Wi-Fi plus Bluetooth design all four share. Plugs that explain this clearly on the listing scored higher. We also noted that Bluetooth range is short, so it supports pairing more than long-distance control.

howWeEvaluated.title: Space efficiency
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared how much of a wall outlet each plug uses. The Govee Dual Smart Plug leads by putting two plugs in the footprint of one outlet. The others use a conventional single plug body, which can crowd a duplex.

howWeEvaluated.title: Voice and app control
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked voice support and scheduling on each listing. Alexa and Google Assistant are named across the family, and the Govee Smart Plug 4 Pack and Govee Smart Plug 15A Group Control highlight group controllers. The Govee Dual Smart Plug notes some conditions for voice use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value for the use case
howWeEvaluated.description: We matched each plug to a clear job. The Govee Smart Plug with Energy Monitoring suits the data-curious, the Govee Dual Smart Plug suits crowded walls, and the Govee Smart Plug 4 Pack suits general use. Value meant fit to a need rather than the longest feature list.

cards.label: Standard design
cards.text: A standard plug covers one socket and controls one device. The Govee Smart Plug 4 Pack, the Govee Smart Plug 15A Group Control and the Govee Smart Plug with Energy Monitoring follow this pattern. It is simple, familiar and works well on spread-out walls. Choose it when you have free outlets and one device per outlet.

cards.label: Dual design
cards.text: The Govee Dual Smart Plug puts two horizontally placed plugs into one housing, so a vertical outlet only loses one socket. You control two devices separately from one slot. It suits desks, bedsides and entertainment corners where outlets are scarce. Choose it when space, not budget, is the limit.

howToChoose.note: Standard for open walls, dual for tight corners.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for group control, schedules, and a rating that covers your light strings. A plug with Bluetooth helps when outdoor extension cords reach awkward spots. Make sure the lights switch on when power returns. Fewer apps beats more features for a once-a-year task.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Govee Smart Plug 15A Group Control and Govee Smart Plug 4 Pack both feature group control, which is the most useful tool here. The Govee Dual Smart Plug fits when two light strings share one outlet. The Govee Smart Plug with Energy Monitoring can show how much power a big display draws.

howToChoose.intro: Spend more on features you will use, not features that sound clever.

faq.q: Which Govee smart plug should I choose first?
faq.a: For most people the Govee Smart Plug 4 Pack is the sensible start, because it covers the basics and lets you add groups later. Move to the Govee Smart Plug with Energy Monitoring if you want usage data. Pick the Govee Dual Smart Plug when outlets are scarce. All of them share the same app, so you can mix models.

faq.q: Do Govee plugs work without Wi-Fi?
faq.a: They support Bluetooth as well as Wi-Fi, which helps with pairing and nearby control. Remote control from away still depends on Wi-Fi. The Govee Smart Plug 4 Pack and the other models in this guide use both connections. Bluetooth range is limited, so do not expect it to cover the whole house.

faq.q: What does energy monitoring actually show?
faq.a: The Govee Smart Plug with Energy Monitoring reports the power, current and voltage of the connected device in the Govee Home app. That helps you see which items draw more than you expected. It is most useful on appliances left running for long periods. For a simple lamp, the numbers are interesting but rarely change what you do.

faq.q: Is the dual plug worth it?
faq.a: It is worth it when outlet space is the problem. The Govee Dual Smart Plug controls two devices while covering only one slot in a vertical outlet. If your walls have plenty of free sockets, a standard plug is simpler. Check the body size against nearby furniture before you buy.

faq.q: Can I use these with Alexa and Google at the same time?
faq.a: Yes, the family lists support for both Alexa and Google Assistant. You set the plug up in the Govee Home app and then link each assistant. The Govee Dual Smart Plug notes some conditions for voice use, so read those steps. Most households only need one assistant.

faq.q: Are these safe for space heaters?
faq.a: Be careful with heat-producing appliances, and avoid them unless a plug clearly covers the load. The Govee Dual Smart Plug and Govee Smart Plug 15A Group Control list 15A, which suits lamps, fans and small appliances. Check the appliance's wattage against the plug's rating. When in doubt, plug heaters straight into the wall.

faq.q: How many plugs do I really need?
faq.a: Count the devices you will automate, not the ones you might someday. A bedroom lamp and a fan need two. A living room with decorations may use four. Because Govee sells one, two and four plug counts, you can start small and add more later.
